title: Tableau VizQL View Render Latency
dataSources: Tableau Server logs (`tableau:backgrounder`, `tableau:vizqlserver`, `tableau:httpd`), `workgroup` repository tables (`background_jobs`, `http_requests`, `_views_stats`, `licensing`) via DB Connect, Tableau Cloud Admin Insights / Activity Log exports.
app: Splunk DB Connect (Splunkbase 2686) against the Tableau Server `workgroup` PostgreSQL repository; Tableau Server logs via Universal Forwarder; Tableau Server REST API and TSM metrics via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=tableau:httpd
| rex field=uri_path "/views/(?<workbook>[^/]+)/(?<view>[^/?]+)"
| where isnotnull(view)
| stats count as loads, avg(time_taken) as avg_ms, p95(time_taken) as p95_ms by workbook, view
| eval p95_s=round(p95_ms/1000,2)
| where p95_s>10
| sort - p95_s
description: Parses the Tableau gateway access log to compute per-view render latency and flags dashboards whose 95th-percentile load time exceeds 10 seconds.
value: Slow dashboards drive users away from self-service analytics; per-view latency shows exactly which content frustrates users so it can be optimised or re-architected.
implementation: Ingest `tableau:httpd`; extract workbook/view from the request path. Schedule daily and review the slowest views with content owners; correlate with VizQL session counts.
visualization: Table of workbook/view with p95 latency, heat map of slow views, trend line.
grandmaExplanation: We time how long each Tableau dashboard takes to open for people so the sluggish ones can be fixed before users give up on them.
